summary: Iteration 52 — Distance Throw Tracker (/throws) + Lifetime Vault (/vault). Backend pytest 3/3 PASS on test_iteration52.py (haversine within 1%, 2000ft sanity cap, vault summary shape). Frontend: auth gate, throw tracker geolocation flow (299.1 ft logged for stubbed ~300 ft coords), offline queue (badge appears when /api/throws aborted, badge count drops to 0 after Sync now), and Lifetime Vault empty state all verified end-to-end against the preview URL as a fresh Firebase user. One minor UX bug found in the offline sync flow — see frontend_issues.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking the 'Sync now' link on the offline-badge, the offline queue is flushed and the badge disappears (count → 0) but the history list is NOT refreshed — the previously-offline throw only appears on the next page reload (useEffect calls flushOffline → load on mount). The request spec explicitly says 'count drops to 0 and history refreshes with the previously-offline throw'. Fix: call `await load()` inside flushOffline() when `ok > 0`, e.g. `if (ok) { toast.success(...); await load(); }`.

issues: The 'Add a profile photo' onboarding modal appears immediately after signup and persists across route changes (/throws, /vault) until dismissed — it blocks pointer events on the underlying page. Not a Iteration-52 regression (pre-existing modal), but worth noting because it caused the Throw Tracker start button click to be intercepted the first run. Consider making the modal per-route dismissible or non-blocking.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/pages/ThrowTracker.jsx › flushOffline(), call `await load()` after a successful sync so history refreshes with the previously-offline throw (spec requirement).
OPTIONAL: gate the 'Add a profile photo' onboarding modal to /feed and /profile only — right now it can spawn over /throws and /vault and block interactions.
critical_code_review_comments: throws_router.py haversine — good: server re-computes and stores its own value, ignoring the client_distance_ft claim. 2000ft cap and coordinate range check both enforced.
vault_router.py — good: excludes _id, groups by (course::hole) so hole 3 at different courses don't mix, tolerates missing par via fallback of 3. `total > 0` filter cleanly hides in-progress cards.
ThrowTracker.jsx — offline queue write/read is wrapped in try/catch for quota; good. Minor: flushOffline should trigger load() after successful drain (see action item).
LifetimeVault.jsx — clean. Uses Web Share API with clipboard fallback and Sonner toast; year/month sort descending as expected.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 52 acceptance suite: /throws + /vault. Backend pytest lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration52.py (still 3/3 green). If retesting the offline-sync fix, use `page.route('**/api/throws', r => r.abort())` after auth is set, complete a throw (expect offline-badge count=1), unroute, click the 'Sync now' button inside the badge, then assert `[data-testid="throw-history"] li` count increased by 1 WITHOUT a page reload. Firebase Identity Toolkit sometimes rate-limits — pytest signup has a 6-retry/15s backoff already. Remember to dismiss the 'Add a profile photo' onboarding modal (button text 'Skip for now') that pops after signup, otherwise it swallows the first click on /throws.
rca of the issue: flushOffline() in ThrowTracker.jsx exits after writing the survivors array and emitting a toast — it never re-fetches /api/throws. On page mount the useEffect chains flushOffline → load, which is why history looks correct on reload but not on the manual 'Sync now' tap. One-line fix: add `await load();` inside the `if (ok)` branch of flushOffline.
